title: Measuring & Managing Community Orgs, Developer Relations and Beyond

reader_summary.headline: Hi everyone, welcome to the Sixth and Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi everyone, welcome to the Sixth and Z podcast. Today's episode continues our community practices series by covering all things developer relations, but it actually applies to almost any company with a community. The discussion covers how to measure the success of community initiatives, including, is there one key metric or KPI for healthy communities.

key_points.text: The discussion covers how to measure the success of community initiatives, including, is there one key metric or KPI for healthy communities.
key_points.evidence_quote: The discussion covers how to measure the success of community initiatives, including, is there one key metric or KPI for healthy communities, and how do you even know you're measuring the right thing, to how to organize dev rel within a community, from who to hire first, where it fits in an organization, how to align incentives, and more.

key_points.text: The conversation also touches on the difference between evangelism and advocacy, the role of meta-communities or community leaders and how to involve them.
key_points.evidence_quote: The conversation also touches on the difference between evangelism and advocacy, the role of meta-communities or community leaders and how to involve them, and where swag does and doesn't come in.

key_points.text: Our guest is Amir Shavat, who is VP of product and developer experience at Twitch at the time this event took place.
key_points.evidence_quote: Our guest is Amir Shavat, who is VP of product and developer experience at Twitch at the time this event took place, was formerly director of developer relations at Slack, and also previously worked at Google and Microsoft.

key_points.text: He begins with a short overview of key concepts, followed by a Q&A with Michael Rogers.
key_points.evidence_quote: He begins with a short overview of key concepts, followed by a Q&A with Michael Rogers, who works on community operations at Protocol Labs, and was formerly community manager of the Node.js Foundation.

thesis: The episode argues that developer relations is a high-cost, one-way decision that most startups do not require unless they are building a platform where developers create value. It further contends that successful developer relations must shift from one-way evangelism to bi-directional advocacy, where teams measure outcomes like 'mean time to hello world' rather than vanity metrics like registered users.
